extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians / commutative algebraists) who need to compute and inspect graded resolutions via the gradedModules.lib library
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for the SINGULAR library procedure TestGRRes: how to call it, what inputs it expects, and what outputs/diagnostics it prints when computing, testing, ordering and transposing a graded resolution of an ideal. Includes example invocations and sample printed output (graded resolutions, homomorphism matrices with degree tables, Betti numbers, transpose, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: TestGRRes(name, I), string name, ideal I
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure is called with two arguments: a string Name and an ideal I. Example: TestGRRes(Name, I);

rubrics_metrics.name: Return value
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure does not return a value to the caller; its effect is to compute and print/test the resolution and related diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / overall goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: compute/test/output/order/transpose a graded resolution of I
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documented intent is to compute a graded resolution for the ideal I, run tests, output the result, order maps/modules, and produce a transpose of the resolution when requested/appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library dependency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure belongs to the gradedModules.lib library; callers should load this library before using TestGRRes. Example code shows LIB "gradedModules.lib"; at top of example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example invocation pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Example shows constructing a ring R and an ideal I, setting string Name = "castelnuovo"; then calling TestGRRes(Name, I);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate typical pre-call setup: define modulus @p, ring R = (@p),(x,y,z,u,v), dp; define the ideal I (long polynomial list); then call TestGRRes(Name, I); followed by cleanup kill R, Name, @p;

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed output: Graded resolution structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed lines such as: 'Graded resolution:' followed by module chain e.g. R <-- d_1 -- R(-4)^2 + R(-5)^4 + R(-6)^3 <-- d_2 -- ... <-- d_n -- 0, given by maps:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure prints the free modules in each homological position (including grading shifts R(a)) and the differential labels d_i; this conveys the structure of the graded free resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed output: Graded homomorphism maps as matrices
rubrics_metrics.description: For each differential, printed blocks like 'd_k : Graded homomorphism: R(...) <- R(...), given by a matrix, with degrees:'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each map in the resolution is displayed as an explicit matrix; immediately following are degree annotations/tables indicating the degrees of source/target basis elements and nonzero entries. Examples in the documentation show the matrix-degree tables and row/column degree markings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed output: Degree tables for maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines and tables labelled with degrees, e.g. 'with degrees:' and column/row degree tables (e.g. '.1 .2 .3 ...', '4 : -', '5 : 2', etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The output annotates matrix rows/columns with degrees and prints counts of entries per degree; users can inspect these tables to understand shifts and where nonzero entries occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed output: Non-minimal Betti numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure prints 'Its non-minimal betti numbers:' (or 'Non-minimal betti numbers:' in examples) and then Betti number tables and totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TestGRRes reports Betti numbers (possibly non-minimal) for the resolution it computed; examples show the Betti vectors and a 'total:' line. Users can read these to assess rank of free modules per homological degree and whether the resolution is minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed output: Degrees of (ordered) maps
rubrics_metrics.description: The documentation prints a section labelled '= Degrees of (ordered) maps:' followed by per-degree tallies, e.g. '0: 1: 2:' and then entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TestGRRes prints degree-ordered data describing the graded pieces of the maps; this helps verify grading consistency and locate where map entries live.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transpose and TRANSPOSE’d complex output
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure (or helper) prints 'Graded transpose of the previous resolution' and shows the transposed graded resolution (e.g. R(9)^2 <-- ...), with its own maps and degree tables and also prints '= TRANSPOSE’d complex:' summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A graded transpose of the computed resolution is produced/displayed so users can inspect dualized/transpose complexes; the documentation shows both the original resolution and its graded transpose output format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbosity / printed markers in examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Example outputs include markers like '==============================================', '=== Example: [ castelnuovo ]', '= Resolution via 'grres':', and other separators to indicate stages of output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The printed output is verbose and segmented; users should scan for these markers to find the resolution, Betti numbers, degree tables, transpose, and other diagnostic sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment / state handling note (assumeLevel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example code manipulates an 'assumeLevel' variable: 'if( defined(assumeLevel) ){ int assumeLevel0 = assumeLevel; } else { int assumeLevel; export(assumeLevel); }; assumeLevel = 5; // store the state of aL'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example shows adjusting environment/global settings (assumeLevel) before calling the procedure; users should be aware of and preserve such state if their workflow depends on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations about input complexity and randomness
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples note 'note: data from random generation' and use large explicit polynomial ideals (long lists) to illustrate typical complex inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TestGRRes is intended to operate on realistically large and complicated ideals; example ideals demonstrate typical usage on nontrivial test data (random or constructed).
